=== apl-values/prod/apps/llzReconciler/kustomization.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run

=== apl-values/prod/apps/llzReconciler/llz-reconciler-env-patch.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` — the per-env REGION_SHORT (volume-labels),
# REGION/OBJ_CLUSTER/OBJ_LABEL_PREFIX (linode-creds) + GH_REPO (apl-overlay)
# for the llz reconciler.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: llz-reconciler
  namespace: llz-reconciler
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: reconcile
          env:
            - name: REGION_SHORT
              value: "pro"
            - name: REGION
              value: "prod"
            - name: OBJ_CLUSTER
              value: "us-ord-7"
            - name: GH_REPO
              value: "akamai-consulting/goldeninst"
            # The instance's Object Storage label prefix. The in-cluster rotator
            # matches keys and buckets by EXACT label, and it has no instance repo
            # to read the spec from — so this is the only way the prefix reaches
            # it. Without it the rotator would fall back to a shared constant and
            # rotate another instance's credentials (clusterspec/objlabels.go).
            - name: OBJ_LABEL_PREFIX
              value: "goldeninst"

=== apl-values/prod/apps/observability/otel-collector-tls-san-patch.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` — the per-env otel.<env>.internal SAN for the OTel
# Collector serving cert (replaces spec.dnsNames wholesale; CR lists are atomic).
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1

metadata:
  name: platform-otel-collector-tls
  namespace: llz-observability
spec:
  dnsNames:
    - otel.prod.internal
    - platform-otel-collector.llz-observability.svc
    - platform-otel-collector.llz-observability.svc.cluster.local
=== apl-values/prod/manifest/env-revision-configmap.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` — the git revision this env's in-repo Argo CD
# content tracks (read by cluster-bootstrap; must equal apps_repo_revision).
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: env-revision
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    config.kubernetes.io/local-config: "true"
data:
  revision: main
=== apl-values/prod/manifest/instance-custom.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run
# `llz render`. See docs/landing-zone-spec.md.
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: instance-custom
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "10"
spec:
  # LOAD-BEARING, AND THE ONLY THING HOLDING THIS PROMISE UP: removing a directory from
  # git must ORPHAN its resources, never tear down running workloads.
  #
  # Mechanism (verified in argo-cd source, not inferred from the field's godoc — which is
  # wrong, see below): this flag is implemented in the RENDER path
  # (applicationset/utils/utils.go), not a deletion path. When true, the controller never
  # puts resources-finalizer on a generated Application; deleteInCluster then does a plain
  # Delete, and Argo only cascades to cluster resources when CascadedDeletion() sees that
  # finalizer. So BOTH deletion routes preserve resources: the whole ApplicationSet being
  # deleted, and a single directory disappearing from the generator's results.
  #
  # Do NOT credit prune:false below for this — pruning governs sync-time diffing, not the
  # deletion cascade. And do not quote the field's godoc ("these Applications will not be
  # deleted"): the Applications ARE deleted; only their resources survive.
  #
  # TWO WAYS TO SILENTLY ARM DESTRUCTION — both fail closed to data loss, neither is
  # caught by any test of ours that does not assert on this manifest:
  #   1. Flipping this to false (or dropping it). The finalizer is re-applied to EXISTING
  #      apps on the next reconcile (the controller force-syncs generated finalizers), so
  #      destruction is armed retroactively, with no git change and no sync.
  #   2. Declaring ANY finalizer in the template below. The render only adds
  #      resources-finalizer when the template has none, so a template finalizer voids
  #      this flag entirely (upstream's own test: "user-specified finalizer should
  #      overwrite preserveResourcesOnDeletion").
  syncPolicy:
    preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  generators:
    # namespaces/<ns>/ → one App per directory, synced into <ns>.
    - git:
        repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
        revision: HEAD
        directories:
          - path: kubernetes-custom/namespaces/*
    # global/ → cluster-scoped resources. Basename is "global", so this generates
    # instance-custom-global, synced into the default namespace (cluster-scoped
    # content needs no namespace of its own); the top-level template below picks
    # the default for this generator by basename.
    #
    # NO per-generator template — deliberately. An earlier revision set one here to
    # repoint only the destination namespace, trusting mergeGeneratorTemplate
    # (mergo.Merge, zero-value fill) to inherit metadata/project/source from the
    # top-level template. But that merge is a CONTROLLER-runtime step; the
    # ApplicationSet CRD validates each generator's template at ADMISSION first and
    # requires template.metadata AND template.spec.project on ANY template block — so
    # a partial one is rejected outright ("spec.generators[1].git.template.spec.project:
    # Required value") and the ENTIRE ApplicationSet never applies (platform-bootstrap
    # retries the invalid object forever while staying Healthy — the silent gap
    # assert-instance-custom exists to catch). Keep generators template-free and choose
    # the destination namespace in the single top-level template instead.
    - git:
        repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
        revision: HEAD
        directories:
          - path: kubernetes-custom/global
  template:
    metadata:
      # No sync-wave here: generated Applications are created by the ApplicationSet
      # controller, not synced by an app-of-apps, so a wave on them gates nothing. The
      # wave that matters is the one on the ApplicationSet itself (above).
      name: instance-custom-{{.path.basename}}
    spec:
      revisionHistoryLimit: 3
      project: instance-custom
      source:
        repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
        path: '{{.path.path}}'
        targetRevision: HEAD
        # Recurse so subdirectories are organizational only — App Platform's semantics
        # ("ArgoCD reconciles everything found there").
        #
        # Setting a directory source at all makes this EXPLICITLY the directory type:
        # ApplicationSource.ExplicitType() keys off source.Directory != nil, and
        # GetAppSourceType returns on the explicit type, so Argo's kustomize
        # auto-detection never runs. A kustomization.yaml under this path would NOT be
        # built — findManifests' manifest regex matches it like any other yaml, and Argo
        # would try to apply a literal Kustomization object to the cluster. That is why
        # llz render / llz doctor reject a kustomization.yaml anywhere under the escape
        # hatch (custom_layout.go): the two are mutually exclusive, and recursion is the
        # behavior App Platform's convention documents. Operators who want kustomize
        # drop their own Argo CD Application pointing at a kustomize root — the same
        # route the Helm/OCI escape uses.
        directory:
          recurse: true
      destination:
        server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
        # global/ (basename "global") → the default namespace for cluster-scoped
        # resources; every namespaces/<ns>/ dir → its own <ns>. Chosen here in the one
        # top-level template (goTemplate) so no generator needs a partial template of
        # its own — a per-generator template omitting metadata/spec.project fails the
        # ApplicationSet CRD's admission validation and blocks the whole object.
        namespace: '{{ if eq .path.basename "global" }}default{{ else }}{{ .path.basename }}{{ end }}'
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: false
          selfHeal: true
        retry:
          limit: 5
          backoff:
            duration: 5s
            maxDuration: 3m
            factor: 2
        syncOptions:
          - ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
          - SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true
          - ServerSideApply=true
          - CreateNamespace=true
=== apl-values/prod/manifest/kustomization.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run
# `llz render`. See docs/landing-zone-spec.md.
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/manifest?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
  - instance-custom.yaml
  - llz-externalsecrets.yaml
  - llz-observability.yaml
  - llz-reconciler.yaml
components:
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/components/certManagerBootstrapCA?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/components/imageSignature?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/components/openbao?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
=== apl-values/prod/manifest/llz-externalsecrets.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run
# `llz render`. See docs/landing-zone-spec.md.
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: llz-externalsecrets
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    # App-level wave: the floor for this App's content, ordered against the other
    # carved Apps (externalSecrets lowest). See clusterspec CarvedApp.AppWave.
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-10"
    # Diff against a server-side-apply DRY RUN, not against the raw manifest, so
    # cluster-written fields (ESO/Kyverno CRD defaults) and admission-webhook
    # rewrites (mutateDigest → image digest) stop reading as unresolvable drift.
    # See clusterspec.CompareOptions for the full why, and why NOT ignoreDifferences.
    argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: ServerSideDiff=true,IncludeMutationWebhook=true
  finalizers:
    - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
spec:
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  project: platform-bootstrap
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
    targetRevision: main
    path: apl-values/prod/apps/externalSecrets
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: external-secrets
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      # prune + selfHeal mirror platform-bootstrap: the carved content stays in
      # lockstep with git, but a transient empty render can't cascade (SSA below).
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
    retry:
      # Same ~1h first-boot budget as platform-bootstrap: wave-5 ExternalSecrets
      # wait on the out-of-band OpenBao unseal -> eso role -> store Ready chain.
      limit: 40
      backoff:
        duration: 15s
        factor: 2
        maxDuration: 90s
    syncOptions:
      - ServerSideApply=true
      # The bundle may carry a CR whose CRD another App installs (ExternalSecret,
      # ServiceMonitor); don't abort the sync dry-running a not-yet-registered kind.
      - SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true
      # cluster-foundation (wave -20) owns the namespaces; don't create/own them here.
      - CreateNamespace=false

=== apl-values/staging/manifest/instance-custom.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run
# `llz render`. See docs/landing-zone-spec.md.
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: instance-custom
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "10"
spec:
  # LOAD-BEARING, AND THE ONLY THING HOLDING THIS PROMISE UP: removing a directory from
  # git must ORPHAN its resources, never tear down running workloads.
  #
  # Mechanism (verified in argo-cd source, not inferred from the field's godoc — which is
  # wrong, see below): this flag is implemented in the RENDER path
  # (applicationset/utils/utils.go), not a deletion path. When true, the controller never
  # puts resources-finalizer on a generated Application; deleteInCluster then does a plain
  # Delete, and Argo only cascades to cluster resources when CascadedDeletion() sees that
  # finalizer. So BOTH deletion routes preserve resources: the whole ApplicationSet being
  # deleted, and a single directory disappearing from the generator's results.
  #
  # Do NOT credit prune:false below for this — pruning governs sync-time diffing, not the
  # deletion cascade. And do not quote the field's godoc ("these Applications will not be
  # deleted"): the Applications ARE deleted; only their resources survive.
  #
  # TWO WAYS TO SILENTLY ARM DESTRUCTION — both fail closed to data loss, neither is
  # caught by any test of ours that does not assert on this manifest:
  #   1. Flipping this to false (or dropping it). The finalizer is re-applied to EXISTING
  #      apps on the next reconcile (the controller force-syncs generated finalizers), so
  #      destruction is armed retroactively, with no git change and no sync.
  #   2. Declaring ANY finalizer in the template below. The render only adds
  #      resources-finalizer when the template has none, so a template finalizer voids
  #      this flag entirely (upstream's own test: "user-specified finalizer should
  #      overwrite preserveResourcesOnDeletion").
  syncPolicy:
    preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  generators:
    # namespaces/<ns>/ → one App per directory, synced into <ns>.
    - git:
        repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
        revision: HEAD
        directories:
          - path: kubernetes-custom/namespaces/*
    # global/ → cluster-scoped resources. Basename is "global", so this generates
    # instance-custom-global, synced into the default namespace (cluster-scoped
    # content needs no namespace of its own); the top-level template below picks
    # the default for this generator by basename.
    #
    # NO per-generator template — deliberately. An earlier revision set one here to
    # repoint only the destination namespace, trusting mergeGeneratorTemplate
    # (mergo.Merge, zero-value fill) to inherit metadata/project/source from the
    # top-level template. But that merge is a CONTROLLER-runtime step; the
    # ApplicationSet CRD validates each generator's template at ADMISSION first and
    # requires template.metadata AND template.spec.project on ANY template block — so
    # a partial one is rejected outright ("spec.generators[1].git.template.spec.project:
    # Required value") and the ENTIRE ApplicationSet never applies (platform-bootstrap
    # retries the invalid object forever while staying Healthy — the silent gap
    # assert-instance-custom exists to catch). Keep generators template-free and choose
    # the destination namespace in the single top-level template instead.
    - git:
        repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
        revision: HEAD
        directories:
          - path: kubernetes-custom/global
  template:
    metadata:
      # No sync-wave here: generated Applications are created by the ApplicationSet
      # controller, not synced by an app-of-apps, so a wave on them gates nothing. The
      # wave that matters is the one on the ApplicationSet itself (above).
      name: instance-custom-{{.path.basename}}
    spec:
      revisionHistoryLimit: 3
      project: instance-custom
      source:
        repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
        path: '{{.path.path}}'
        targetRevision: HEAD
        # Recurse so subdirectories are organizational only — App Platform's semantics
        # ("ArgoCD reconciles everything found there").
        #
        # Setting a directory source at all makes this EXPLICITLY the directory type:
        # ApplicationSource.ExplicitType() keys off source.Directory != nil, and
        # GetAppSourceType returns on the explicit type, so Argo's kustomize
        # auto-detection never runs. A kustomization.yaml under this path would NOT be
        # built — findManifests' manifest regex matches it like any other yaml, and Argo
        # would try to apply a literal Kustomization object to the cluster. That is why
        # llz render / llz doctor reject a kustomization.yaml anywhere under the escape
        # hatch (custom_layout.go): the two are mutually exclusive, and recursion is the
        # behavior App Platform's convention documents. Operators who want kustomize
        # drop their own Argo CD Application pointing at a kustomize root — the same
        # route the Helm/OCI escape uses.
        directory:
          recurse: true
      destination:
        server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
        # global/ (basename "global") → the default namespace for cluster-scoped
        # resources; every namespaces/<ns>/ dir → its own <ns>. Chosen here in the one
        # top-level template (goTemplate) so no generator needs a partial template of
        # its own — a per-generator template omitting metadata/spec.project fails the
        # ApplicationSet CRD's admission validation and blocks the whole object.
        namespace: '{{ if eq .path.basename "global" }}default{{ else }}{{ .path.basename }}{{ end }}'
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: false
          selfHeal: true
        retry:
          limit: 5
          backoff:
            duration: 5s
            maxDuration: 3m
            factor: 2
        syncOptions:
          - ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
          - SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true
          - ServerSideApply=true
          - CreateNamespace=true
=== apl-values/staging/manifest/kustomization.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run
# `llz render`. See docs/landing-zone-spec.md.
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/manifest?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
  - instance-custom.yaml
  - llz-externalsecrets.yaml
  - llz-observability.yaml
  - llz-harbor.yaml
  - llz-reconciler.yaml
components:
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/components/certManagerBootstrapCA?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/components/imageSignature?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
  - github.com/akamai-consulting/lke-landing-zone//platform-apl/components/openbao?ref=v0.0.0-golden&timeout=80
=== apl-values/staging/manifest/llz-externalsecrets.yaml
# GENERATED by `llz render` from the LandingZone spec — DO NOT EDIT.
# Toggle components via spec.components in environments/<env>.yaml, then re-run
# `llz render`. See docs/landing-zone-spec.md.
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: llz-externalsecrets
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    # App-level wave: the floor for this App's content, ordered against the other
    # carved Apps (externalSecrets lowest). See clusterspec CarvedApp.AppWave.
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-10"
    # Diff against a server-side-apply DRY RUN, not against the raw manifest, so
    # cluster-written fields (ESO/Kyverno CRD defaults) and admission-webhook
    # rewrites (mutateDigest → image digest) stop reading as unresolvable drift.
    # See clusterspec.CompareOptions for the full why, and why NOT ignoreDifferences.
    argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: ServerSideDiff=true,IncludeMutationWebhook=true
  finalizers:
    - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
spec:
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  project: platform-bootstrap
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/akamai-consulting/goldeninst.git
    targetRevision: main
    path: apl-values/staging/apps/externalSecrets
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: external-secrets
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      # prune + selfHeal mirror platform-bootstrap: the carved content stays in
      # lockstep with git, but a transient empty render can't cascade (SSA below).
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
    retry:
      # Same ~1h first-boot budget as platform-bootstrap: wave-5 ExternalSecrets
      # wait on the out-of-band OpenBao unseal -> eso role -> store Ready chain.
      limit: 40
      backoff:
        duration: 15s
        factor: 2
        maxDuration: 90s
    syncOptions:
      - ServerSideApply=true
      # The bundle may carry a CR whose CRD another App installs (ExternalSecret,
      # ServiceMonitor); don't abort the sync dry-running a not-yet-registered kind.
      - SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true
      # cluster-foundation (wave -20) owns the namespaces; don't create/own them here.
      - CreateNamespace=false

--- terraform-iac-bootstrap/cluster/encryption.tf  sha256=8373b7b3e232d0e93a985d12d36e6855bea62a3a872d64efa447cb257df90e8c  bytes=3563

=== terraform-iac-bootstrap/cluster/prod.tfvars
cluster_label = "platform-prod"
region = "us-ord"

# OpenBao HA topology for this deployment. The default is a self-contained,
# single-cluster OpenBao — most deployments want this:
ha_role = "standalone"
ha_group = ""
# For a two-cluster HA pair, give BOTH deployments the same ha_group and opposite
# roles, e.g. in <active>.tfvars: ha_role = "active" ha_group = "prod"
# in <standby>.tfvars: ha_role = "standby" ha_group = "prod"
# `llz env list --ha`, `llz env role <name>`, and `llz env peer <name>` read
# these to drive the OpenBao dual-write, cross-region CA, and Harbor seeding.

# Code-promotion pipeline position is NOT set here — it lives in the LandingZone
# spec as `cluster.promotionRank` (set it with `llz env add --promotion-rank` or in
# environments/<env>.yaml). `llz env list --ordered` / `llz env next <name>` read it
# straight from the spec; Terraform never consumes it. See
# docs/environments-and-promotion.md.

# Update this to a currently supported LKE Enterprise version in your account.
k8s_version = "v1.33.6+lke7"

# Optional tags applied to the cluster/pool/firewall/VPC. The spec
# (spec.cluster.tags) is the source of truth and overrides this when set; an
# empty base means an instance that declares no tags is not stamped with leftover
# example labels. e.g. tags = ["team-x", "prod"]
tags = []

# Node pool sizing for apl-core's full stack (istio, keycloak, argocd,
# cert-manager, ESO, CNPG, kube-prometheus-stack, Loki, Harbor, kyverno, trivy).
# g7-premium-4 ×3 (24 GB) is the documented floor — g7-premium-2 ×3 (12 GB) left
# argocd Pending on "Insufficient memory".
#
# Do NOT bump this to g7-premium-8 (16 GB ea) without first confirming the target
# Linode account's instance/vCPU quota: g7-premium-8 ×3 = 24 vCPU / 48 GB hung
# cluster creation indefinitely on the e2e account (nodes never provisioned →
# `linode_lke_cluster` "Still creating…" to the job timeout). preflight-quota.sh
# only checks for ORPHANS, not the requested pool vs the account limit, so it
# won't catch an over-quota pool. node_type is ForceNew — changing it recreates
# the pool.
#
# node_count = 5, NOT 3: apl-core's full stack already fills 3× g8-dedicated-8-4,
# and once the support-plane deploys (OpenBao HA ×3 + ESO + Argo Workflows/Events
# + cert-automation + the internal-CIDR firewall) the 2nd/3rd OpenBao replicas go
# Pending — "Insufficient memory" on 2 nodes and "max volume count" on the 3rd —
# stalling Bootstrap OpenBao. 5 nodes give the memory headroom and spread PVCs
# under the per-Linode Block Storage attach limit. (node_count is NOT ForceNew —
# it just scales the pool.)
node_type = "g8-dedicated-8-4"
node_count = 5

control_plane_high_availability = true
control_plane_audit_logs_enabled = true

# Control-plane ACL: who may reach the LKE Kubernetes API server (TCP 443).
# Terraform seeds the ACL at cluster-create from the github_runner_* CIDRs below
# so the bootstrapping runner can reach the API server. After init, the
# in-cluster cloud-firewall-controller owns the ACL — it resolves the EAA/bastion
# CIDRs from the Linode firewall template via the Linode API and reconciles them
# (with a committed firewall_rules/ fallback) every cycle. There is no
# control_plane_acl_enabled/control_plane_acl_ipv4 variable at this root.
#
# Operator/VPN/CI egress CIDRs that must reach the API server and node NodePorts.
# Do NOT use 0.0.0.0/0.
github_runner_ipv4_cidrs = [] # e.g. ["203.0.113.0/24"]
github_runner_ipv6_cidrs = []

autoscaler_enabled = false
# Pool bounds — only consulted when autoscaler_enabled = true. Uncomment to
# override the 3/6 default (spec: cluster.nodePool.autoscalerMin/autoscalerMax).
# autoscaler_min = 3
# autoscaler_max = 6

# Managed App Platform: true → Linode installs+manages apl-core + provisions the
# akamai-apl.net domain (bootstrap-cluster skips its own apl-core install). ADR 0005.
apl_enabled = false
--- terraform-iac-bootstrap/cluster/providers.tf  sha256=2718a1c8896f90d6d167e4d5ee2d536928fe895c090ee6331c295a60260fb189  bytes=276

region = "us-sea"

# Do NOT use 0.0.0.0/0.
github_runner_ipv4_cidrs = [] # e.g. ["203.0.113.0/24"]

autoscaler_enabled = false
# Pool bounds — only consulted when autoscaler_enabled = true. Uncomment to
# override the 3/6 default (spec: cluster.nodePool.autoscalerMin/autoscalerMax).
# autoscaler_min = 3
# autoscaler_max = 6

--- terraform-iac-bootstrap/databases/encryption.tf  sha256=8373b7b3e232d0e93a985d12d36e6855bea62a3a872d64efa447cb257df90e8c  bytes=3563

=== terraform-iac-bootstrap/databases/prod.tfvars
# databases — the VPC-attached Linode Managed PostgreSQL clusters for this
# deployment: zero, one, or several. Downstream app platforms carve per-app
# logical DBs + roles out of a cluster (e.g. Crossplane provider-sql), reaching
# it over the VPC. The admin credentials are seeded into OpenBao at
# `secret/platform/db-admin/<name>` by `llz ci seed-db-admin` at bootstrap —
# never committed.
#
# terraform apply -var-file=<env>.tfvars
#
# Per-env separation is the backend state key (-backend-config at init), NOT a
# terraform workspace.
#
# Copy to <env>.tfvars (lab | staging | primary | secondary | <your-env>).

# Deployment suffix — must match the matching cluster deployment.
region_suffix = "prod"

# The clusters, keyed by name. The key is both the label segment
# ("platform-<name>-<region_suffix>") and the state address
# (module.databases["<name>"]), so adding or removing one leaves the others
# untouched.
#
# EMPTY IS THE DEFAULT AND A VALID DEPLOYMENT: apply provisions nothing. That is
# how `databases` stays opt-in — `llz render` writes this file for every env
# whether or not the instance wants a database.
#
# Per entry:
# region (required) Linode geographic region — MUST match the VPC's region.
# vpc_id (required) VPC to attach to; VPC-only, no public endpoint.
# Typically the same VPC the LKE cluster attaches to.
# subnet_id (required) Subnet within vpc_id.
# linode-cli vpcs list
# linode-cli vpcs subnets-list <vpc_id>
# engine_version (optional, "16") Major PostgreSQL version. When MIGRATING data
# in, set at least the source's major version —
# pg_restore is forward-compatible only.
# db_type (optional, "g6-dedicated-2") linode-cli databases types
# cluster_size (optional, 2) 1 = single node, 2/3 = HA with standbys.
#
# Example — one shared cluster plus a separately-sized one:
#
# databases = {
# shared = {
# region = "us-ord"
# vpc_id = 575244
# subnet_id = 12345
# }
# analytics = {
# region = "us-ord"
# vpc_id = 575244
# subnet_id = 12345
# db_type = "g6-dedicated-8"
# cluster_size = 1
# }
# }
databases = {}

# ── SECRET — supply via TF_VAR_* env var, NOT in this file ────────────────────
# TF_VAR_linode_token Linode account API token (databases:read_write)
label_prefix = "goldeninst"

=== terraform-iac-bootstrap/object-storage/prod.tfvars
# object-storage — Linode Object Storage buckets (registry + logs). Consumed by
# Harbor and Loki. Buckets only: the scoped access keys are minted by
# `llz ci mint-bootstrap-objkeys` and rotated in-cluster, never by Terraform.
#
# terraform apply -var-file=<env>.tfvars
#
# Per-env separation is the backend state key (-backend-config at init), NOT a
# terraform workspace.
#
# Copy to <env>.tfvars (lab | staging | primary | secondary | <your-env>).

# Deployment suffix — must match the matching cluster deployment.
region_suffix = "prod"

# Per-instance namespace on every bucket label — `llz render` fills this from
# spec.instance.objLabelPrefix. Bucket labels are GLOBAL per region on Linode, so
# two instances sharing a prefix collide on "[400] ... already exists".
label_prefix = "goldeninst"

# Linode Object Storage cluster ID. List options with:
# linode-cli object-storage clusters-list
obj_cluster = "us-ord-7"

# ── SECRET — supply via TF_VAR_* env var, NOT in this file ────────────────────
# TF_VAR_linode_token Linode account API token (object-storage:read_write)
